subject: Contract rollforward: premium support & capacity uplift proposal
messages:
From: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Tue, 30 Jan 2029 09:12:00 -0800
Subject: Aperture contract rollforward & premium support options

Hi Lisa —

Following up on our renewal window: Aperture's current term is up in June and we've put together two paths that meet the capacity and latency goals you outlined during Q4. Quick summary:

- Option A: 12-month rollforward, committed capacity x2 baseline, standard support (24/5) — 9% list discount
- Option B: 12-month rollforward, committed capacity x2 baseline, Premium SLA (99.95% latency SLO, 24/7 priority ops), faster incident SLAs, onboarding credits — 16% list discount + $30k implementation credit

I've attached the draft SOW (Aperture_Renewal_SOW_v2.pdf) with the estimated monthly MRR and a simple uplifts table. I wanted to loop Sofia in as the account lead to propose a workable timeline and Marissa for contract coordination.

If Option B sounds like the direction, we can ship a formal amendment + DocuSign and include a 30-day staged ramp for the extra capacity to avoid traffic spikes.

Next steps I suggest: you confirm which option, reply with any internal procurement/legal contacts, and we’ll produce the amendment and pricing workbook.

Thanks —
Ben Carter
Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
(Attachment: Aperture_Renewal_SOW_v2.pdf)

From: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@aperturehealth.com>
To: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Cc: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 31 Jan 2029 10:23:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aperture contract rollforward & premium support options

Ben —

Thanks for the options. A few practical questions from procurement before we escalate to legal:

1) Can you provide committed QPS and TPS numbers tied to the x2 uplift? Need concrete thresholds for our capacity planning.
2) For Option B, what is the exact SLA language you propose for latency SLOs (p50/p90/p99 targets) and what credits apply if SLOs are missed?
3) We will need a clean redline set for our counsel (I'll attach a procurement questionnaire).
4) Pricing: can you send a line-item pricing spreadsheet showing on-demand vs committed unit pricing across the 12 months?

If you can get that by next Tue (6 Feb) we can fast-track to legal and funding approval. Our legal lead (cc'd in later messages) will take care of contract redlines.

Regards,
Lisa Gomez
Head of Procurement, Aperture Health
(Attachment: procurement_questionnaire.xlsx)

From: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
To: Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@aperturehealth.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>, Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 12 Feb 2029 11:02:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aperture contract rollforward & premium support options

Hi Lisa —

Appreciate the clear ask. I pulled the ops and pricing teams together and here's a concrete amendment proposal we can put on paper this week to unblock approvals:

- Term: 12 months (rollforward from current expiry)
- Capacity: committed 2.0× baseline (committed QPS: 12k sustained; burst to 30k for 3 windows/day)
- SLA: Premium Support package — 99.95% availability & latency SLO targets (p50: 30ms, p90: 120ms, p99: 450ms) measured at the API gateway; financial credits tiered (see attached pricing workbook)
- Pricing: Effective committed unit price $0.0026/token (committed), $0.0038/token (burst) — net 16% off list when signed by 28 Feb
- Credits: $30,000 onboarding credit applied against first two invoices; two-week migration assistance included
- Ops: 24/7 priority channel, named escalation path, one quarterly performance review and monthly token-level cost reports

Attachments: Aperture_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf (updated MRR schedule) and a pricing spreadsheet link. We'll prepare the amendment + DocuSign link as soon as you confirm the capacity numbers above and confirm internal legal contact.

I can jump on a 30-min call tomorrow to walk through the SLO definitions if helpful.

Thanks —
Sofia Ivanova
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
(Attachments: Aperture_Renewal_SOW_v3.pdf)

Sofia/Ben —

Thanks for the detail. Our counsel ran a quick pass and attached a redline with a couple of asks:

- Data Processing Addendum required (we need standard DPA + SCCs)
- Clarify incident SLA credit calculation (we asked for a cap on cumulative credits at 6 months' MRR)
- Request a 60-day notice for scheduled maintenance impacting the API SLA

I've attached our redline PDF and a proposed timing: we'd like the amendment signed by 28 Feb to align with our budget cycle. Could you give us a short summary of any material legal exceptions Redwood would need to accept?

Regards,
Victor Chen
Senior Counsel, Aperture Health
(Attachment: Aperture_Redlines_v1.pdf)

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
To: Victor Chen <v.chen@aperturehealth.com>, Lisa Gomez <lisa.gomez@aperturehealth.com>, Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: Ben Carter <ben.carter@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 14 Feb 2029 15:03:00 -0800
Subject: Re: Aperture contract rollforward & premium support options

Victor/Lisa —

Appreciate the redline — we've reviewed and can accommodate most items. Quick summary of Redwood positions:

- DPA: we can execute Redwood's standard DPA and are open to incorporating SCCs. I'll have our privacy counsel send the DPA draft by EOD Thu.
- Credit cap: we can accept a cumulative credit cap but propose a slightly lower cap at 3 months' MRR (vs your 6 months) for severe SLA breaches; open to negotiation and we can surface the financial impact in the amendment appendix.
- Maintenance notice: 60-day notice is reasonable for planned maintenance that materially affects API availability — we'll add language and an exclusion for emergency mitigations tied to security incidents.

I attached a response redline (redwood_response_redlines.docx) with the proposed language. If that looks acceptable I can have the amendment and DocuSign packet ready today for signature.

Can we do a 20-min alignment call this afternoon at 4pm PT to finalize outstanding points?

Best,
Marissa Cole
Deputy General Counsel, Redwood Inference
(Attachment: redwood_response_redlines.docx)
